methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.

original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: On the published two-edge feed, every D-exponent (0,-1) correction of the sharp owner index from PR #7033 leaves coefficient 1 on the x1 monomial Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3 D1 D3. The corrections that keep x0 = D1 Q^{-1} and y0 zero are exactly u1 = -u0 C1, u2 = -u0 x, u3 = 0 for an arbitrary D-exponent-0 element u0. Their x1 column is that monomial plus u0 times a fixed three-monomial defect. One bank forces u0 = 0. The four banks stay stored. No new kappa.
scope_change_reason: The card allows one source-bound caller identity or an obstruction to that change. This package does not change the query demand and does not rerun the D-exponent-0 obstruction of PR #7033, the y0 defect, or the one-edge C1 Q result. It answers the D-exponent (0,-1) term named by that PR, including every bank coefficient of that same exponent.
bottleneck_link: An autonomous main row needs x1 = 0 with x0 = D1 Q^{-1} and y0 = 0. Every formal D-exponent (0,-1) correction of the sharp index leaves the residual monomial's coefficient equal to 1, so this term does not earn a new kappa.
stop_rule: Stop once every D-exponent (0,-1) correction of the sharp index is shown to keep coefficient 1 on the residual monomial, including the boundary-preserving family. Do not solve a D-exponent (0,1) correction or a physical quotient.
evidence: PROOF.md and verify.py. The four transported x1 columns miss D degree (1,1), and a D-exponent-0 factor preserves degree. The boundary family is the closed form u1=-u0 C1, u2=-u0 x, u3=0. The syllable-length-4 replay is a control, not a census of u0. No kappa change.

open_questions.question: Can a D-exponent (0,1) correction of the same sharp index, using two or more banks, make the fresh x1 column zero while keeping x0 = D1 Q^{-1} and y0 zero?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Exponent (0,-1) never meets the residual degree. One homogeneous term on one bank is already blocked for every degree by the monomial gate, but two banks at exponent (0,1) can meet x1 degree (1,0) and therefore degree (1,1).
open_questions.first_step: Use the coefficient shape u1 = -u0 C1, u2 = -u0 x, u3 = 0, which keeps the boundary at D3 as well as at D3^{-1}. For u0 = I the degree-(1,1) line properly contains the residual. Decide whether any D-exponent-0 u0 makes R + u0 Delta_+ the zero element, and charge every monomial of a solution.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package classifies only exponent (0,-1), plus the one-bank gate for a single homogeneous degree. The positive-power defect is not solved.
